    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>In Enter the Gungeon, this white distorted rectangle icon appeared after I cleared a room in floor 1:</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6Z1BC.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="Mini map icon" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6Z1BC.png"/></a></p>
<p>The room looks empty and the icon on the mini map seems to correspond to the walls in the center:</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/Pawnd.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="Full game screenshot" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/Pawnd.png"/></a></p>
<p>So what does this icon mean?</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>In Enter the Gungeon, this white distorted rectangle icon appeared after I cleared a room in floor 1:</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6Z1BC.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="Mini map icon" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6Z1BC.png"/></a></p>
<p>The room looks empty and the icon on the mini map seems to correspond to the walls in the center:</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/Pawnd.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="Full game screenshot" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/Pawnd.png"/></a></p>
<p>So what does this icon mean?</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });

<p>I've been getting into old arcade games recently and recently came across someone saying that performance on the original games are in fact better, but is that actually true? From what I've gathered emulated games tend to run smoother due to the better way games in general run and I cannot see how a game made in the 1960s could run even remotely better than what modern technology can run arcade games such as Pac Man and Q*Bert.</p>
<p>Am I just not seeing the facts and the original games are better than the emulated games?</p>
</div>

<div class="comment-text js-comment-text-and-form">
<div class="comment-body js-comment-edit-hide">
<span class="comment-copy">Depends how you measure performance. Yes, you can add all the motion blur, anti-aliasing and 120fps to Pac-Man, but that's not really authentic. Preference will also account too, similar to how a lot of people prefer listening to music on vinyl as opposed to CD or even mp3, including old music where the sound has been digitally cleaned up. Also, there is a huge gamut of arcade games, from Pong to Halo: Fireteam Raven. Some machines are easy to emulate, and others not (for instance, while not arcade, the Sega Saturn used to be notoriously difficult).</span>
<div class="d-inline-flex ai-center">
– <a class="comment-user" href="/users/245734/user25730" title="151 reputation">user25730</a>

    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<p>I've been getting into old arcade games recently and recently came across someone saying that performance on the original games are in fact better, but is that actually true? From what I've gathered emulated games tend to run smoother due to the better way games in general run and I cannot see how a game made in the 1960s could run even remotely better than what modern technology can run arcade games such as Pac Man and Q*Bert.</p>
<p>Am I just not seeing the facts and the original games are better than the emulated games?</p>
</div>

<div class="comment-text js-comment-text-and-form">
<div class="comment-body js-comment-edit-hide">
<span class="comment-copy">Depends how you measure performance. Yes, you can add all the motion blur, anti-aliasing and 120fps to Pac-Man, but that's not really authentic. Preference will also account too, similar to how a lot of people prefer listening to music on vinyl as opposed to CD or even mp3, including old music where the sound has been digitally cleaned up. Also, there is a huge gamut of arcade games, from Pong to Halo: Fireteam Raven. Some machines are easy to emulate, and others not (for instance, while not arcade, the Sega Saturn used to be notoriously difficult).</span>
<div class="d-inline-flex ai-center">
– <a class="comment-user" href="/users/245734/user25730" title="151 reputation">user25730</a>

            location = 1;

            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });

            });

<p>I've been getting into old arcade games recently and recently came across someone saying that performance on the original games are in fact better, but is that actually true? From what I've gathered emulated games tend to run smoother due to the better way games in general run and I cannot see how a game made in the 1960s could run even remotely better than what modern technology can run arcade games such as Pac Man and Q*Bert.</p>
<p>Am I just not seeing the facts and the original games are better than the emulated games?</p>

<div class="comment-text js-comment-text-and-form">
<div class="comment-body js-comment-edit-hide">
<span class="comment-copy">Depends how you measure performance. Yes, you can add all the motion blur, anti-aliasing and 120fps to Pac-Man, but that's not really authentic. Preference will also account too, similar to how a lot of people prefer listening to music on vinyl as opposed to CD or even mp3, including old music where the sound has been digitally cleaned up. Also, there is a huge gamut of arcade games, from Pong to Halo: Fireteam Raven. Some machines are easy to emulate, and others not (for instance, while not arcade, the Sega Saturn used to be notoriously difficult).</span>
<div class="d-inline-flex ai-center">

<p>I've been getting into old arcade games recently and recently came across someone saying that performance on the original games are in fact better, but is that actually true? From what I've gathered emulated games tend to run smoother due to the better way games in general run and I cannot see how a game made in the 1960s could run even remotely better than what modern technology can run arcade games such as Pac Man and Q*Bert.</p>
<p>Am I just not seeing the facts and the original games are better than the emulated games?</p>

<div class="comment-text js-comment-text-and-form">
<div class="comment-body js-comment-edit-hide">
<span class="comment-copy">Depends how you measure performance. Yes, you can add all the motion blur, anti-aliasing and 120fps to Pac-Man, but that's not really authentic. Preference will also account too, similar to how a lot of people prefer listening to music on vinyl as opposed to CD or even mp3, including old music where the sound has been digitally cleaned up. Also, there is a huge gamut of arcade games, from Pong to Halo: Fireteam Raven. Some machines are easy to emulate, and others not (for instance, while not arcade, the Sega Saturn used to be notoriously difficult).</span>
<div class="d-inline-flex ai-center">
– <a class="comment-user" href="/users/245734/user25730" title="151 reputation">user25730</a>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<p>I've been getting into old arcade games recently and recently came across someone saying that performance on the original games are in fact better, but is that actually true? From what I've gathered emulated games tend to run smoother due to the better way games in general run and I cannot see how a game made in the 1960s could run even remotely better than what modern technology can run arcade games such as Pac Man and Q*Bert.</p>
<p>Am I just not seeing the facts and the original games are better than the emulated games?</p>

<div class="comment-text js-comment-text-and-form">
<div class="comment-body js-comment-edit-hide">
<span class="comment-copy">Depends how you measure performance. Yes, you can add all the motion blur, anti-aliasing and 120fps to Pac-Man, but that's not really authentic. Preference will also account too, similar to how a lot of people prefer listening to music on vinyl as opposed to CD or even mp3, including old music where the sound has been digitally cleaned up. Also, there is a huge gamut of arcade games, from Pong to Halo: Fireteam Raven. Some machines are easy to emulate, and others not (for instance, while not arcade, the Sega Saturn used to be notoriously difficult).</span>
<div class="d-inline-flex ai-center">

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<p>I've been getting into old arcade games recently and recently came across someone saying that performance on the original games are in fact better, but is that actually true? From what I've gathered emulated games tend to run smoother due to the better way games in general run and I cannot see how a game made in the 1960s could run even remotely better than what modern technology can run arcade games such as Pac Man and Q*Bert.</p>
<p>Am I just not seeing the facts and the original games are better than the emulated games?</p>

<div class="comment-text js-comment-text-and-form">
<div class="comment-body js-comment-edit-hide">
<span class="comment-copy">Depends how you measure performance. Yes, you can add all the motion blur, anti-aliasing and 120fps to Pac-Man, but that's not really authentic. Preference will also account too, similar to how a lot of people prefer listening to music on vinyl as opposed to CD or even mp3, including old music where the sound has been digitally cleaned up. Also, there is a huge gamut of arcade games, from Pong to Halo: Fireteam Raven. Some machines are easy to emulate, and others not (for instance, while not arcade, the Sega Saturn used to be notoriously difficult).</span>
<div class="d-inline-flex ai-center">

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<p>I've been getting into old arcade games recently and recently came across someone saying that performance on the original games are in fact better, but is that actually true? From what I've gathered emulated games tend to run smoother due to the better way games in general run and I cannot see how a game made in the 1960s could run even remotely better than what modern technology can run arcade games such as Pac Man and Q*Bert.</p>
<p>Am I just not seeing the facts and the original games are better than the emulated games?</p>

<div class="comment-text js-comment-text-and-form">
<div class="comment-body js-comment-edit-hide">
<span class="comment-copy">Depends how you measure performance. Yes, you can add all the motion blur, anti-aliasing and 120fps to Pac-Man, but that's not really authentic. Preference will also account too, similar to how a lot of people prefer listening to music on vinyl as opposed to CD or even mp3, including old music where the sound has been digitally cleaned up. Also, there is a huge gamut of arcade games, from Pong to Halo: Fireteam Raven. Some machines are easy to emulate, and others not (for instance, while not arcade, the Sega Saturn used to be notoriously difficult).</span>
<div class="d-inline-flex ai-center">

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<p>I've been getting into old arcade games recently and recently came across someone saying that performance on the original games are in fact better, but is that actually true? From what I've gathered emulated games tend to run smoother due to the better way games in general run and I cannot see how a game made in the 1960s could run even remotely better than what modern technology can run arcade games such as Pac Man and Q*Bert.</p>
<p>Am I just not seeing the facts and the original games are better than the emulated games?</p>

<div class="comment-text js-comment-text-and-form">
<div class="comment-body js-comment-edit-hide">
<span class="comment-copy">Depends how you measure performance. Yes, you can add all the motion blur, anti-aliasing and 120fps to Pac-Man, but that's not really authentic. Preference will also account too, similar to how a lot of people prefer listening to music on vinyl as opposed to CD or even mp3, including old music where the sound has been digitally cleaned up. Also, there is a huge gamut of arcade games, from Pong to Halo: Fireteam Raven. Some machines are easy to emulate, and others not (for instance, while not arcade, the Sega Saturn used to be notoriously difficult).</span>
<div class="d-inline-flex ai-center">

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<p>I've been getting into old arcade games recently and recently came across someone saying that performance on the original games are in fact better, but is that actually true? From what I've gathered emulated games tend to run smoother due to the better way games in general run and I cannot see how a game made in the 1960s could run even remotely better than what modern technology can run arcade games such as Pac Man and Q*Bert.</p>
<p>Am I just not seeing the facts and the original games are better than the emulated games?</p>

<div class="comment-text js-comment-text-and-form">
<div class="comment-body js-comment-edit-hide">
<span class="comment-copy">Depends how you measure performance. Yes, you can add all the motion blur, anti-aliasing and 120fps to Pac-Man, but that's not really authentic. Preference will also account too, similar to how a lot of people prefer listening to music on vinyl as opposed to CD or even mp3, including old music where the sound has been digitally cleaned up. Also, there is a huge gamut of arcade games, from Pong to Halo: Fireteam Raven. Some machines are easy to emulate, and others not (for instance, while not arcade, the Sega Saturn used to be notoriously difficult).</span>
<div class="d-inline-flex ai-center">

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>There are some caves that has these chests behind the revolving statues. Standing on the platform rotates and you end up on the other platform, rather than the other side of the wall.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6IBFA.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="chest behind the revolving statues" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6IBFA.jpg"/></a></p>
<p>How do I get to the other side?</p>
<p>Tried a number of things, like using lumos (light) on while on the platform and nothing I've tried worked.</p>
<p>I believe there's multiple locations of this setup, one is across the lake from Hogwarts, south of Aranshire.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/fkKV3.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/fkKV3.jpg"/></a></p>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've gone there and solved it!</p>
<p>You'll need Glacius magic (the one that freezes enemies and some thing).</p>
<p>You have to use that magic to the brazier, and the fire will be extinguished, so it makes the statue to rotate, and voila you'll be able to take the chests.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EOWsqgHgq6w" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Took a video of it</a>, if you want to see how it works.</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>There are some caves that has these chests behind the revolving statues. Standing on the platform rotates and you end up on the other platform, rather than the other side of the wall.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6IBFA.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="chest behind the revolving statues" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6IBFA.jpg"/></a></p>
<p>How do I get to the other side?</p>
<p>Tried a number of things, like using lumos (light) on while on the platform and nothing I've tried worked.</p>
<p>I believe there's multiple locations of this setup, one is across the lake from Hogwarts, south of Aranshire.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/fkKV3.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/fkKV3.jpg"/></a></p>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've gone there and solved it!</p>
<p>You'll need Glacius magic (the one that freezes enemies and some thing).</p>
<p>You have to use that magic to the brazier, and the fire will be extinguished, so it makes the statue to rotate, and voila you'll be able to take the chests.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EOWsqgHgq6w" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Took a video of it</a>, if you want to see how it works.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>There are some caves that has these chests behind the revolving statues. Standing on the platform rotates and you end up on the other platform, rather than the other side of the wall.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6IBFA.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="chest behind the revolving statues" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6IBFA.jpg"/></a></p>
<p>How do I get to the other side?</p>
<p>Tried a number of things, like using lumos (light) on while on the platform and nothing I've tried worked.</p>
<p>I believe there's multiple locations of this setup, one is across the lake from Hogwarts, south of Aranshire.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/fkKV3.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/fkKV3.jpg"/></a></p>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've gone there and solved it!</p>
<p>You'll need Glacius magic (the one that freezes enemies and some thing).</p>
<p>You have to use that magic to the brazier, and the fire will be extinguished, so it makes the statue to rotate, and voila you'll be able to take the chests.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EOWsqgHgq6w" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Took a video of it</a>, if you want to see how it works.</p>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>There are some caves that has these chests behind the revolving statues. Standing on the platform rotates and you end up on the other platform, rather than the other side of the wall.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6IBFA.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="chest behind the revolving statues" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6IBFA.jpg"/></a></p>
<p>How do I get to the other side?</p>
<p>Tried a number of things, like using lumos (light) on while on the platform and nothing I've tried worked.</p>
<p>I believe there's multiple locations of this setup, one is across the lake from Hogwarts, south of Aranshire.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/fkKV3.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/fkKV3.jpg"/></a></p>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've gone there and solved it!</p>
<p>You'll need Glacius magic (the one that freezes enemies and some thing).</p>
<p>You have to use that magic to the brazier, and the fire will be extinguished, so it makes the statue to rotate, and voila you'll be able to take the chests.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EOWsqgHgq6w" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Took a video of it</a>, if you want to see how it works.</p>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>There are some caves that has these chests behind the revolving statues. Standing on the platform rotates and you end up on the other platform, rather than the other side of the wall.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6IBFA.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="chest behind the revolving statues" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6IBFA.jpg"/></a></p>
<p>How do I get to the other side?</p>
<p>Tried a number of things, like using lumos (light) on while on the platform and nothing I've tried worked.</p>
<p>I believe there's multiple locations of this setup, one is across the lake from Hogwarts, south of Aranshire.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/fkKV3.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/fkKV3.jpg"/></a></p>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've gone there and solved it!</p>
<p>You'll need Glacius magic (the one that freezes enemies and some thing).</p>
<p>You have to use that magic to the brazier, and the fire will be extinguished, so it makes the statue to rotate, and voila you'll be able to take the chests.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EOWsqgHgq6w" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Took a video of it</a>, if you want to see how it works.</p>
</div>

    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });

<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>There are some caves that has these chests behind the revolving statues. Standing on the platform rotates and you end up on the other platform, rather than the other side of the wall.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6IBFA.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="chest behind the revolving statues" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6IBFA.jpg"/></a></p>
<p>How do I get to the other side?</p>
<p>Tried a number of things, like using lumos (light) on while on the platform and nothing I've tried worked.</p>
<p>I believe there's multiple locations of this setup, one is across the lake from Hogwarts, south of Aranshire.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/fkKV3.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/fkKV3.jpg"/></a></p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've gone there and solved it!</p>
<p>You'll need Glacius magic (the one that freezes enemies and some thing).</p>
<p>You have to use that magic to the brazier, and the fire will be extinguished, so it makes the statue to rotate, and voila you'll be able to take the chests.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EOWsqgHgq6w" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Took a video of it</a>, if you want to see how it works.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>There are some caves that has these chests behind the revolving statues. Standing on the platform rotates and you end up on the other platform, rather than the other side of the wall.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6IBFA.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="chest behind the revolving statues" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6IBFA.jpg"/></a></p>
<p>How do I get to the other side?</p>
<p>Tried a number of things, like using lumos (light) on while on the platform and nothing I've tried worked.</p>
<p>I believe there's multiple locations of this setup, one is across the lake from Hogwarts, south of Aranshire.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/fkKV3.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/fkKV3.jpg"/></a></p>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've gone there and solved it!</p>
<p>You'll need Glacius magic (the one that freezes enemies and some thing).</p>
<p>You have to use that magic to the brazier, and the fire will be extinguished, so it makes the statue to rotate, and voila you'll be able to take the chests.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EOWsqgHgq6w" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Took a video of it</a>, if you want to see how it works.</p>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>There are some caves that has these chests behind the revolving statues. Standing on the platform rotates and you end up on the other platform, rather than the other side of the wall.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6IBFA.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="chest behind the revolving statues" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6IBFA.jpg"/></a></p>
<p>How do I get to the other side?</p>
<p>Tried a number of things, like using lumos (light) on while on the platform and nothing I've tried worked.</p>
<p>I believe there's multiple locations of this setup, one is across the lake from Hogwarts, south of Aranshire.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/fkKV3.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/fkKV3.jpg"/></a></p>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've gone there and solved it!</p>
<p>You'll need Glacius magic (the one that freezes enemies and some thing).</p>
<p>You have to use that magic to the brazier, and the fire will be extinguished, so it makes the statue to rotate, and voila you'll be able to take the chests.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EOWsqgHgq6w" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Took a video of it</a>, if you want to see how it works.</p>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>There are some caves that has these chests behind the revolving statues. Standing on the platform rotates and you end up on the other platform, rather than the other side of the wall.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6IBFA.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="chest behind the revolving statues" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/6IBFA.jpg"/></a></p>
<p>How do I get to the other side?</p>
<p>Tried a number of things, like using lumos (light) on while on the platform and nothing I've tried worked.</p>
<p>I believe there's multiple locations of this setup, one is across the lake from Hogwarts, south of Aranshire.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/fkKV3.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/fkKV3.jpg"/></a></p>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've gone there and solved it!</p>
<p>You'll need Glacius magic (the one that freezes enemies and some thing).</p>
<p>You have to use that magic to the brazier, and the fire will be extinguished, so it makes the statue to rotate, and voila you'll be able to take the chests.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EOWsqgHgq6w" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Took a video of it</a>, if you want to see how it works.</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>How do I set a (world)-spawn in the nether, so that when a player dies, they respawn in the nether? I am unwilling to use the trick of moving the nether to the overworld. A respawn anchor is nice, but I want them to keep working even after a few deaths. I also don't want to make glowstone accessible to the player (before reaching the overworld).</p>
<p>The player starts in the nether, and the respawn should work similarly to the world spawn. The player should not be able to 'cheat respawn' their way to the overworld without going there first and setting a bed as spawn.</p>
<p>My idea was to set up a respawn anchor in the nether, and a repeating command block which keeps replacing the respawn anchor with a full one in the overworld spawn chunks. Only this doesn't work for new players.</p>
</div>

    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });

<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>How do I set a (world)-spawn in the nether, so that when a player dies, they respawn in the nether? I am unwilling to use the trick of moving the nether to the overworld. A respawn anchor is nice, but I want them to keep working even after a few deaths. I also don't want to make glowstone accessible to the player (before reaching the overworld).</p>
<p>The player starts in the nether, and the respawn should work similarly to the world spawn. The player should not be able to 'cheat respawn' their way to the overworld without going there first and setting a bed as spawn.</p>
<p>My idea was to set up a respawn anchor in the nether, and a repeating command block which keeps replacing the respawn anchor with a full one in the overworld spawn chunks. Only this doesn't work for new players.</p>
</div>

    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });

<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>How do I set a (world)-spawn in the nether, so that when a player dies, they respawn in the nether? I am unwilling to use the trick of moving the nether to the overworld. A respawn anchor is nice, but I want them to keep working even after a few deaths. I also don't want to make glowstone accessible to the player (before reaching the overworld).</p>
<p>The player starts in the nether, and the respawn should work similarly to the world spawn. The player should not be able to 'cheat respawn' their way to the overworld without going there first and setting a bed as spawn.</p>
<p>My idea was to set up a respawn anchor in the nether, and a repeating command block which keeps replacing the respawn anchor with a full one in the overworld spawn chunks. Only this doesn't work for new players.</p>
</div>

    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });

<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>How do I set a (world)-spawn in the nether, so that when a player dies, they respawn in the nether? I am unwilling to use the trick of moving the nether to the overworld. A respawn anchor is nice, but I want them to keep working even after a few deaths. I also don't want to make glowstone accessible to the player (before reaching the overworld).</p>
<p>The player starts in the nether, and the respawn should work similarly to the world spawn. The player should not be able to 'cheat respawn' their way to the overworld without going there first and setting a bed as spawn.</p>
<p>My idea was to set up a respawn anchor in the nether, and a repeating command block which keeps replacing the respawn anchor with a full one in the overworld spawn chunks. Only this doesn't work for new players.</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>How do I set a (world)-spawn in the nether, so that when a player dies, they respawn in the nether? I am unwilling to use the trick of moving the nether to the overworld. A respawn anchor is nice, but I want them to keep working even after a few deaths. I also don't want to make glowstone accessible to the player (before reaching the overworld).</p>
<p>The player starts in the nether, and the respawn should work similarly to the world spawn. The player should not be able to 'cheat respawn' their way to the overworld without going there first and setting a bed as spawn.</p>
<p>My idea was to set up a respawn anchor in the nether, and a repeating command block which keeps replacing the respawn anchor with a full one in the overworld spawn chunks. Only this doesn't work for new players.</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>How do I set a (world)-spawn in the nether, so that when a player dies, they respawn in the nether? I am unwilling to use the trick of moving the nether to the overworld. A respawn anchor is nice, but I want them to keep working even after a few deaths. I also don't want to make glowstone accessible to the player (before reaching the overworld).</p>
<p>The player starts in the nether, and the respawn should work similarly to the world spawn. The player should not be able to 'cheat respawn' their way to the overworld without going there first and setting a bed as spawn.</p>
<p>My idea was to set up a respawn anchor in the nether, and a repeating command block which keeps replacing the respawn anchor with a full one in the overworld spawn chunks. Only this doesn't work for new players.</p>
</div>
